frontiers.title: Large-model coherence interval
frontiers.question: Does the proposed dimensionless coherence interval [0.5615, 0.8319] hold for independently measured large language models beyond the current small model set?
frontiers.current_understanding: The claim registry records a proposed coherence interval with measurements on six models and no independent 70B+ confirmation.
frontiers.unresolved: The available evidence does not establish that the interval generalizes to large models or architectures outside the current measurement set.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Measure dimensionless tau on at least three 70B+ models; a well-calibrated large model consistently outside the proposed interval across independent runs would falsify the claim as currently stated.
frontiers.next_gate: Run the pending 70B+ measurement program with fixed instrumentation and publish raw measurements and calibration details.

source_refs.purpose: Current claim maturity and evidence boundary.
Registered falsification test and pending hardware dependency.

frontiers.title: Cross-architecture tau scaling
frontiers.question: Is tau approximately proportional to 0.10 × N^0.48 across independent architecture families, or is the observed exponent specific to the current dataset?
frontiers.current_understanding: The claim registry records an empirical scaling fit based on a limited set including GPT-2, Phi-2 and Mistral-7B.
frontiers.unresolved: Independent architecture families and multiple sizes per family have not yet established a cross-architecture exponent.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Measure at least three additional architecture families across multiple sizes; exponent outside [0.43, 0.53] or prefactor outside [0.07, 0.13] on an independent family would falsify the current cross-architecture claim.
frontiers.next_gate: Build a preregistered measurement matrix for Mistral, Falcon and Gemma families and estimate uncertainty around exponent and prefactor.

source_refs.purpose: Current empirical scaling claim and maturity.
Cross-architecture falsification thresholds.

frontiers.title: Operational identity criterion
frontiers.question: Can the LIM statement that identity is what survives boundary-governed transformation over time be restated as an operational, falsifiable criterion without collapsing representation continuity into personal identity?
frontiers.current_understanding: C-LIM-001 is explicitly M0/M1 and the falsification backlog states that it is not falsifiable as currently phrased.
frontiers.unresolved: There is no operational definition that yields a yes/no test for identity across a boundary-governed transformation.
contradictions: The claim is presently meaningful as conceptual framing but cannot yet carry empirical standing.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: First define an operational criterion and a transformation test protocol; until that exists, no empirical falsification is available.
frontiers.next_gate: Produce competing operational definitions that preserve the representation/person distinction and identify discriminating test cases for each.

source_refs.purpose: Explicit M0/M1 status and person-boundary warning.
Registered requirement for operational reformulation.

frontiers.title: LIM-to-VALO bridge necessity
frontiers.question: Which, if any, LIM-derived principles are actually necessary for VALO governance invariants rather than merely explanatory or structurally analogous?
frontiers.current_understanding: C-LIM-002 records a structural bridge between Tofoo meaning and VALO execution, but the dependency has not been formally tested.
frontiers.unresolved: It is unknown whether VALO retains all governance invariants when LIM-derived constraints are removed from the analysis.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Demonstrate a VALO runtime or formal model that preserves its governance invariants without any LIM-derived constraint; that would falsify necessity as currently stated.
frontiers.next_gate: Construct a dependency matrix separating descriptive analogy from constraints that are demonstrably required by VALO invariants.

frontiers.title: Fleet-routing PoA denominator
frontiers.question: What is the correct social-welfare objective for the fleet-routing model, and does it support PoA = 1.2622?
frontiers.current_understanding: The backlog records that the standard denominator yields PoA = 6.09, while 1.2622 is recoverable only under an ungrounded interpretation C.
frontiers.unresolved: The denominator corresponding to the true social-welfare objective has not been derived and justified.
contradictions: The registered 1.2622 value conflicts with the standard-denominator calculation of 6.09.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Derive the social-welfare objective from the demand model. If it is the standard x_opt·l(x_opt) objective, the 1.2622 claim fails.
frontiers.next_gate: Specify the demand model and derive the welfare denominator from first principles before further PoA claims are promoted.

frontiers.title: Post-toll global optimality
frontiers.question: Does the proposed Pigouvian toll actually recover the global social optimum, or is post-toll PoA = 1 false outside the local derivation?
frontiers.current_understanding: The falsification backlog records that current CTMC simulation indicates the global-optimality claim does not hold and labels the claim likely false.
frontiers.unresolved: A formal global proof or corrected simulation has not closed the claim.
contradictions: Existing CTMC evidence points against the post-toll PoA = 1 claim.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Provide a formal global optimality proof or a corrected CTMC experiment. Continued failure to recover the global optimum falsifies the claim.
frontiers.next_gate: Reproduce the CTMC result independently, fix the objective definition from FG-005, and either retire or restate C-FR-006.

frontiers.title: J-space adaptive sweep mechanism
frontiers.question: Do controlled broad-scan, target-lock and disconfirming conditions produce distinct J-space reorganization followed by a stable decision-relevant candidate set?
frontiers.current_understanding: The claim is conceptual/protocol-level. A deterministic falsifier and synthetic mechanics tests exist, but the empirical J-lens run is still pending and synthetic success is explicitly not evidence for the claim.
frontiers.unresolved: The proposed workspace-selection mechanism has not been demonstrated on instrumented real-model traces beyond lexical or non-J-space controls.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Run preregistered matched J-lens experiments. Failure of target concentration, counterevidence recruitment, workspace reorganization or repeated candidate stabilization beyond controls falsifies the claim.
frontiers.next_gate: Execute the preregistered multi-task J-lens experiment with matched lexical/task and non-J-space controls and preserve raw per-layer/token sparse coordinates.

frontiers.title: J-space stability versus spectral coherence
frontiers.question: Do stable decision-relevant J-space candidate sets and tau inside the configured Goldilocks regime co-occur more reliably for coherent reasoning than matched failure controls?
frontiers.current_understanding: The existing harness keeps J-space candidate stability and P10 tau coupling independently falsifiable; the paired empirical run is pending.

frontiers.title: Framleis continuity under legitimate novelty
frontiers.question: Can representation-continuity checks distinguish surprising but legitimate novelty from adversarial lineage drift better than simpler predictability or anomaly baselines?
frontiers.current_understanding: C-FRL-001 separates predictability from representation continuity and records the distinction as conceptual/schema-level; no preregistered legitimate-novelty benchmark exists yet.
frontiers.unresolved: The practical value of provenance, lineage, amendment basis and representation invariants has not been measured against simpler anomaly baselines on surprising changes.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: On a preregistered benchmark, if continuity checks cannot distinguish legitimate surprising changes from adversarial drift better than simpler predictability/anomaly baselines, the claim fails.
frontiers.next_gate: Design a benchmark containing predictable changes, surprising legitimate amendments, silent rewrites, poisoning and cumulative drift, with blinded continuity adjudication.

source_refs.purpose: Current Framleis continuity-versus-predictability claim and explicit benchmark gap.

frontiers.title: Future compositional reach as a retention signal
frontiers.question: Does target-independent marginal semantic closure gain predict future compositional capability beyond finite Boolean construction and outperform immediate utility, generic diversity and random retention on pristine task families?
frontiers.current_understanding: Synapse R22 found no generic distribution-level advantage for max-min semantic diversity. R23 then recovered 23 exact cases across frozen budgets versus 13 for diversity and a 19.33 hash-random mean by selecting relations for marginal one-step semantic closure gain.
frontiers.unresolved: The positive result is bounded to deterministic Boolean composition and has not been replicated on a pristine non-Boolean or open semantic task family.
contradictions: Immediate isolated utility and generic max-min diversity were both inadequate future-value proxies in the frozen R22/R23 setting.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Freeze the R23 selector and evaluate it without tuning on at least one pristine task family. Failure to beat both random retention and immediate-utility retention under matched budgets rejects generalization of the proxy.
frontiers.next_gate: Run a preregistered pristine-family replication with the selector, budgets and comparison rules frozen before target exposure.

source_refs.purpose: Bounded positive and negative evidence for retention by future compositional reach.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from Synapse R22/R23 selection and retention results.

frontiers.title: Formation of reliable latent regulatory memory
frontiers.question: How can a system form a useful incomplete regulatory trace before an exact solution is known, without hand-constructing the trace or leaking the future target?
frontiers.current_understanding: Compact regulatory traces can causally bias later regeneration, and learned lineage bias can transfer to related unseen phenotypes. A preregistered pre-solution top-four poising rule was not reliable, making memory formation itself the unresolved mechanism.
frontiers.unresolved: No target-independent formation rule has yet shown reliable held-out benefit when the trace must be created before exact success.
contradictions: Useful partial structure can appear before solution, but the tested top-four formation rule did not preserve it reliably.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: A frozen pre-solution formation rule must beat scratch and matched random traces on held-out targets while remaining incomplete and free of target identifiers; otherwise the candidate rule fails.
frontiers.next_gate: Preregister a formation rule based on partial consequence and future semantic reach, then test it on sealed held-out targets.

source_refs.purpose: Regulatory-memory successes and the preserved negative pre-solution result.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from regulatory-memory formation, transfer and negative-control results.

frontiers.title: Safe forgetting under uncertainty
frontiers.question: What deletion certificate can safely distinguish redundant relation state from uncertain low-utility state in open domains?
frontiers.current_understanding: Conservative retention outperformed policies that treated uncertainty as deletion, and deletion of certified semantic duplicates preserved all represented semantic classes and reconstruction capability under pressure.
frontiers.unresolved: Exact semantic-duplicate certificates are available in the constructed domain but not generally in open semantic research.
contradictions: Low current utility was not evidence of dispensability; relations with low isolated utility were sometimes required for later composition.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Under matched memory pressure, a proposed open-domain certificate must delete state without reducing held-out capability or future compositional coverage relative to no deletion.
frontiers.next_gate: Define an auditable redundancy certificate for one bounded semantic domain and compare it with score-based pruning and conservative retention.

source_refs.purpose: Evidence for conservative retention and certificate-based forgetting.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from conservative latent retention and safe-forgetting experiments.

frontiers.title: Selected identity formation
frontiers.question: Does stable computational identity form by selecting a repeatedly demonstrated phenotype and protecting its minimum causal support, rather than by discovering a target-blind natural structural core?
frontiers.current_understanding: R28 did not find a target-blind natural core. R29 selected a stable five-capability phenotype, derived a minimum four-relation cover from successful episodes and preserved exact continuity across 25 of 25 unseen turnover schedules.
frontiers.unresolved: The result is a bounded relational phenotype, not personal identity, and has not been replicated across rich semantic systems or independently designed environments.
contradictions: Structural centrality alone narrowed breadth and did not identify the demonstrated identity phenotype.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: On a pristine environment, compare selected minimum causal support against target-blind structural cores under turnover. Failure to preserve the chosen phenotype better than controls rejects the mechanism's generality.
frontiers.next_gate: Freeze the R29 formation procedure and replicate it on a separately designed task family with a predeclared phenotype and turnover schedule.

source_refs.purpose: Negative structural-core result and positive selected-identity result.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from R28 structural-core falsification and R29 identity formation.

frontiers.title: Expansion without self-erasure
frontiers.question: Can a formed and protected relational phenotype expand into new capabilities without erasing its existing causal core under fixed capacity and consequence budgets?
frontiers.current_understanding: R30 preserved the resident identity phenotype in 150 of 150 episodes but acquired only three of six new targets. R31 later acquired all six under a different plastic retention regime while preserving 360 of 360 identity episodes.
frontiers.unresolved: The positive expansion result reused the same six targets that shaped the struggle regime and therefore needs a pristine split.
contradictions: Protection alone preserved continuity but did not provide sufficient plastic search.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Freeze the formed core and expansion policy before exposing a pristine target family. Any core regression or failure to improve materially over reset search falsifies the claimed stability-plasticity mechanism.
frontiers.next_gate: Run the frozen R31 policy on a pristine expansion family while retaining exact resident-capability checks throughout learning.

source_refs.purpose: Identity-preserving expansion result and its pristine-split limitation.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from R30 expansion failure and R31 bounded recovery.

frontiers.title: Struggle-driven capability formation
frontiers.question: Does persistent unresolved need plus selective retention of partial consequence form capabilities that reset search misses, without relying on generic overload or target-specific tuning?
frontiers.current_understanding: R31 persistent-retention recovered six of six capabilities, including all three R30 misses, with about 58 percent fewer evaluations and transport than reset. Overload alone did not improve beyond steady persistence.
frontiers.unresolved: The mechanism has not yet been tested on a pristine task family and must not be generalized as a claim that stress improves learning.
contradictions: More pressure alone was insufficient; persistence plus partial-consequence retention carried the observed advantage.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: With the policy frozen, failure to outperform reset on sealed pristine targets under the same aggregate consequence budget rejects generalization of the mechanism.
frontiers.next_gate: Execute the preregistered pristine-family R31 replication without changing retention capacity, ranking or consequence ceilings.

source_refs.purpose: Bounded struggle-driven capability result and required next falsifier.

lineage.change_note: Seeded from the R31 persistent-retention result.

frontiers.title: Representation portability and semantic re-grounding
frontiers.question: Can an incomplete history-derived disposition infer enough semantic binding online to transfer across a new representation without an externally supplied exact bridge?
frontiers.current_understanding: RM-6 preserved lineage-specific developmental choice across 512 fresh mixed invertible representations only when an explicit correct semantic bridge was supplied. Raw-coordinate and misbound controls collapsed toward the symmetric attractor distribution.
frontiers.unresolved: The experiment demonstrates bridge-dependent portability, not representation-free memory or learned semantic translation.
contradictions: Byte persistence and coordinate reuse were insufficient without correct semantic binding.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Provide only bounded paired interaction and consequence evidence in a new representation. A learned bridge must transfer prior disposition better than scratch while wrong or non-identifiable mappings fail closed.
frontiers.next_gate: Run RM-7 with the exact bridge removed and a preregistered bounded semantic re-grounding budget.

source_refs.purpose: Representation-shift result and semantic-bridge boundary.

frontiers.title: Derivation versus legitimate novelty
frontiers.question: Can Twin historical replay reliably classify a candidate as derivation, rediscovery, reframe or legitimate new primitive before the Garden changes represented research state?
frontiers.current_understanding: Twin replay and frozen semantic scoring provide an implemented derivability surface, but secondary review found summary and schema defects and required rework. The collaborative-frontier lanes were specified but not experimentally run.
frontiers.unresolved: The classifier is not yet a validated novelty gate, and a Twin representation cannot decide truth, personhood or authority.
contradictions: Primary scoring was internally reproducible while its release summary and schema still failed secondary review.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Correct the review defects, freeze the rubric and run blinded cases with known derivability lineage. Failure to separate derivation from seeded novelty above simpler baselines rejects use as a Garden gate.
frontiers.next_gate: Resolve the Twin review defects and run the sealed collaborative-frontier matrix with preserved AI, human, joint and new-model provenance.

source_refs.purpose: Twin replay evidence, review defects and unrun frontier protocol.

frontiers.title: Sparse role-diverse frontier swarm
frontiers.question: Does sparse targeted routing across derivation, synapse, falsifier, counterexample and bridge roles preserve rare high-value candidates and improve verified frontier progress over dense broadcast or majority aggregation?
frontiers.current_understanding: External work supports targeted communication and warns that dense hub-dominated communication can collapse higher-order interaction and diversity. Twin defines sterile role-separated lanes, but the Garden swarm comparison has not been run.
frontiers.unresolved: No matched-budget Tofoo experiment has established which topology, role allocation or candidate-preservation rule improves verified research progress.
contradictions: Model agreement is supplementary evidence and generic diversity did not itself guarantee better held-out capability.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: Under sealed matched frontier packets and budgets, sparse role-diverse routing must outperform dense broadcast, independent duplication and majority-only aggregation on preregistered verified progress without suppressing rare falsifiers.
frontiers.next_gate: Run the existing collaborative-frontier protocol with frequency-blind first review and explicit rare-candidate retention.

frontiers.title: Research-state commit versus action authority
frontiers.question: What minimum machine-checkable contract proves that Garden, Twin, Synapse or a learning evaluator may update represented research state without acquiring consequence-bearing execution authority?
frontiers.current_understanding: Tofoo already separates open questions, claims, results, governed state and authority. HCL-style evaluator commit and Research Factory routing are learning or selection operations, while execution authorization remains outside Tofoo.
frontiers.unresolved: The Garden protocol states the boundary, but no repository-local conformance test currently proves that future adapters cannot turn research-state updates into a direct effect path.
frontiers.falsifier_or_decisive_test: A conformance test must demonstrate that every non-informative action path is absent and that Garden packet generation, adjudication and state updates expose no execution credential or authority decision. Any direct effect path fails the contract.
frontiers.next_gate: Define a negative conformance fixture for Garden and Twin adapters that asserts no authority minting, no execution credential and no consequence-bearing tool path.

source_refs.purpose: Canonical separation between research-state commit, routing, evaluation and execution authority.
